title: Build 50 distinct bosses, five modes, seven classes and an in-game changelog
head: feat/first-playable-loop
body:
Expands Grave Accord to fifty executable bosses and five modes. Grand Raid adds seven identities and a three-fight solo-to-sixteen-player route with two unique regulars and a reserved finale. All seven classes, 378 skills, 28 weapons and six distinct map footprints remain connected. The in-game dated journal, repository changelog and fifteen-page Wiki track actual playable behavior.

Raid counterplay uses breakable pylons, sequential rib openings, three independently visible interruptible keepers, neutral F pump valves, four separate throne attendants, broad bite escape lanes, destructible core covers and shelters against inhalation. Protocol 11 shares pull prediction and migrates bounded local protocol-10 saves. Rib/core damage transfers once without duplicate body credit. Adds seventy-two drawn motion poses, eight props and seven original themes; all forty-three previous PCM masters remain unchanged. Twelve native returns, exact requests and two superseded sheets are preserved and independently audited.

Validation: 217 rules/history/WebSocket/HTTP/SQL tests, authored-content/fifteen-locale checks, TypeScript and production build. New checks cover every Raid boss over real WebSockets, sixteen-client admission and seventeenth rejection, complete route budgets, Normal/Brutal phases, neutral objectives, save limits, damage credit and prediction. Actual browser sampling covers Bell Triplets on Ossuary Works and the updated changelog. Exact hashes and limitations are recorded in reviews/runtime-verification.json and separate art/audio/UI reports.

Keep draft and main protected. Ten identities, full Endless-exclusive/secret rules, persistent profiles/mastery/cosmetics, verified rankings, durable online recovery and Windows/offline/LAN packaging remain unfinished. Final human listening, full rendered actions/facings, physical-device/native-language, WAN/endurance and balance acceptance remain open. Public hosting is still its older protocol-4 Site; source/Wiki publication does not redeploy it.
